utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. It is Case Number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Before we hear the witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention to this Bench? Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not off hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have a question to ask you. How many witnesses are there in this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a very short week. We have one witness for today, one witness for Wednesday, and one witness for Thursday. As you recall -- I believe it was a week and a half ago, on Thursday, the Thursday before the long weekend, we were notified late in the afternoon, probably between 5.00 and 6.00 that in addition to Muzenovic being taken off the list, the witnesses that were to follow, which would have been this week on Grabovica, were all to be removed and we were to move the Uzdol case up. We did that. We moved the Uzdol case up. However, we were only able to bring in three witnesses this week. In addition to that, we have for next week seven witnesses. We are going to run two witnesses Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Wednesday could drop down to one because one of the witnesses is pregnant. Thursday, Friday, into the following Monday, I believe, Mr. Karavelic will follow. And then next week will also be a full week of witnesses with another three, right up to the break for the contempt hearing. We apologise but with the very quick switch from the Grabovica to the Uzdol case, we were only able to obtain three witnesses for the week. It's also possible - I can't say it's definite - it's possible that we could even run two days this week, that Wednesday we might be able to place two witnesses on, but I won't be able to let you know probably for another day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. What are you going to do with that pregnant witness? Are you going to drop her from the witness list or are you proposing some other way?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: She is visiting the doctor tomorrow, and we'll have a better idea when she meets her doctor and let the doctor make the decision as to whether or not she's able to travel. We might be able to do a very quick videolink or some other process, whether it's 92 bis or whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And the -- would you please file a list of the witnesses until 22nd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We did very late -- very late -- right around 5.00 on last Friday, so the registrar and legal officer should have it. You'll probably get it sometime this morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. And Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that the other day you mentioned that you have some submissions concerning of the witness Karic's deposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you going to do it now or maybe we could do it sometime later this week? It depends on whether you need some time for preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm -- I had in mind to do it a little later in the week because I knew that the Prosecutors were doing what -- doing the best they could, were unable to fill up the week. So it may be appropriate to do that at a later time. The witness today is one who we could possibly finish today if we get on with it, effectively. So in deference to that, I wasn't planning to raise that today, and I expected to raise it later in the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I raise some other matters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The first one is that as to -- we didn't realise there was a witness who was pregnant, but a person who is pregnant has got a very strong claim on the videolink, I would have thought, Your Honour. The Defence won't create any difficulties about the. The Prosecutor can let us know anyway in due course. The next thing is that my learned friend's advised me over the weekend that the Prosecutor wishes to add some exhibits to the 60 -- to the exhibit list with this witness who are not on the list. Now, those are exhibits which were always part of the Prosecution brief and in fact were annexed to the statement of the witness. And after speaking with Mr. Weiner, we've indicated to him that we agree that the Prosecution -- of course it's up to the Chamber, but the Defence consents to the Prosecutor adding those three -- there maps, and they could assist in one form or another, so we don't reject that. The other thing is, Your Honour, that the Prosecutor has indicated they will lead through this witness some death certificates. And initially I had some Defence paranoia about this, but what I'm told is by the Prosecutor is that this witness he was a local official, and these documents are led through him simply to prove the fact of the death of those people, not cause of death or any medical matters, and on that basis I have got no objection to those being led either. So just so we know in advance that there is no objection to them. I make those points and now I'll stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, as for the videolink witness, I hope we could be informed as early as possible because it will take weeks for the preparation for that videolink. And, Mr. Morrissey, I thank you very much for your cooperation concerning with the exhibits as well as the death certificates for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, having said that, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you state your name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Kazo Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us your age and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: The 24th of February, 1956. I'm about 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm going to go through some questions to move this along quick where we just need a yes or no answer, and they concern some background. And then we'll get to the actual time with you in the HVO military we'll have you give your full answers. You were born Uzdol, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're currently living in Uzdol with your family?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And your family includes your wife and 11 children?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You went to religious school in Prozor and you graduated a school for administration --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, in Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In Split, sorry. And you graduated a school of administration in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You became the village registrar in Uzdol in 1988?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the registrar maintains the records of births, marriages, deaths, and so on?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you were a member of the JNA, a Yugoslav People's Army, for 15 months in 1976 and 1977?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You were mobilised in March/April of 1992 by the HVO army?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You served in logistics?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you delivered meals to the troops as part of your logistics duties?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And finally, during the war you remained in the village as the registrar of Uzdol and a logistics officer where you brought food to the troops?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's move to the beginning of 1993, the end of 1992, beginning of 1993. Where was your family living?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: My family was living in Prozor. My wife and five children were living there, and my parents, myself, and I -- a daughter of mine were living in Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, why was half of your family living in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Well, the war broke out and an order was issued for women and small children to leave the village because of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you remained, though, in Uzdol and you indicated with your parents and which daughter?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Jadranka my eldest daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you live in -- what type of house was it? A house, a farm, an apartment complex? What did you live in?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: It was a family house, a small village house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you describe Uzdol before I show you some pictures, could you describe it to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Well, it's a mountainous place, it has a number of hamlets, Rajici, Cer, a school of Zelenike, Kriz, Pale, Bobari. Budimi. It's a village that has four or five hamlets and a hundred inhabitants in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to show you a paragraph having ERN number 0402-0894.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 298.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see that picture in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us what that picture depicts?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: It depicts the village of Uzdol and part of Here above in the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is that a fair and accurate representation of the school as it existed in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, is there a building known as the school?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you use the special pencil that the usher will give to you. Circle it and put over it a 1 over it, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I've marked it in the circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. And is the church -- do you see the church in the village?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I do. There are two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could -- are they next to each other?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: There's about 50 metres between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you put a 2 between those two churches.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you see your home in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please circle your home and put a 3 over that.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: There's a stable by the house in this new photograph because it had been set on fire before and there's a smokehouse, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your neighbours, the Zelics, can you see their home in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please circle that with a 4.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: The first one is the old one and the other one is -- is the new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did both the old and new homes exist in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. They lived in the old house. They hadn't moved into the new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see the house of Domin Rajic in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please circle that and place a 5.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see the home of the Prkovic family?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The surname isn't quite clear to me. Perkovic. Perkovic, it's not Prkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Oh, Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Perkovic. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you put a 6 next to that. Is that the Grubesas house --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you put a 7 on that, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And finally, can you see the home of Kata and Mato Ljubic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you put a -- an 8 next to that, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The home of Luca and Janja Zelenika; can you see that?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you place a 9 at that house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: This one is Janja's, and the other one can't be seen very well. You can only see Janja's, but the other one is in an orchard so you can't see it well. Number 9, is that the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So 9 will just be Luca's.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Luca's house. And Janja's is that -- they are next to each other, but you can't see it because of the plum trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And finally, Dragica Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you put a 10 next to that house.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd like to offer that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I guess there's no objections so it's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P299.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll -- there's no need, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't object to the admission of the previous photo either. Sorry, I just thought that there were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I thought it was 298, so I don't know if they're going into one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There are two photos. One is the original. That is 29 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: 298, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenika, let's move to September 13th, 1993. Could you tell us where you stayed that night.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: That night I stayed in Prozor with my wife and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, the next morning what time did you get up, as best you can recall?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I got up at about 6.00, perhaps even at 5.00. Someone said that Uzdol was burning and we immediately set off there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you were told that Uzdol was burning?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I was on the balcony of the building I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was the distance between Prozor, where you were, and Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: About 12 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you see anything in the direction of Uzdol after you had heard it was burning?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: You can't see anything from Prozor because Prozor is down below. It's only after you've travelled for about a kilometre from Prozor that you can see Uzdol, and then you could see fire and smoke. There were buildings on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you hear anything from that direction?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: You could hear the sound of shooting, but it's quite far away, but sometimes you could hear the sound of shells exploding. That's from the point from which you can see Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said "we set off for Uzdol" or we set off there, who did you leave with to go to Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I left with Rajic and Slavko Zelenika, my driver. He drove a TAM vehicle. Or a driver who drove a TAM vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, as you drove to Uzdol, did you meet anyone along the way?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: In Perici we met someone. Ivan Stojanovic's child was there, and the child was running along the road and crying. And the child said, They have killed my mother up in Kriz, Anica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did he ever tell you, this child, young Mr. Stojanovic, who had killed his mother?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: He said, Hero Saban has killed my mother. This person died, not in the war but later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you know Hero Saban or Saban Hero?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He worked in Gradina, a company in Prozor called Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you know if he fought in any -- in either of the armies?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that. When he was mobilised, he was probably in the army of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear what the witness said at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who did you say, sir, which army?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: In the BH army. Because we were the HVO and they were the ABiH. I couldn't know who was among their ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said "we were the HVO." What was the ethnic composition of the village of Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: The village of Uzdol is a purely Croatian village. And the other neighbouring villages, Ljubunci, Kranjcici, and Donja Vas, are mixed. And the village of Here, a village in our local commune, was a purely Bosniak village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And of what ethnic group do you belong to, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I'm a Croat myself. There were no Serbs in any of the villages in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you continue on after speaking with Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We drove on to Uzdol. The little one was scared like a child. He drove on towards Prozor and we headed back to Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, where did you eventually arrive in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We arrived at about 7.00, half past 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where did you park?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We parked about two or three kilometres from Uzdol itself towards Kracko Polje, between Kolanusici and Kracko Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what did you do when you parked two to three kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We left the TAM vehicle right there and we walked on along the road. We could see all the villages along the road burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where did you go first in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I first went to Rade Stojanovic's house. We met some civilians who were on the run. Some had been wounded and they were running to Prozor. We passed Mijo Maric's house and reached the north section of the village where the school building used to be. We took a shortcut.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did you observe in the area of the school?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Once we reached Uzdol, I saw a dead body and I recognised Pero Kovcalija who was an HVO soldier. It was lying about 10 metres from a house belonging to a man named Cuba. There was another body there belonging to a Bosniak, a member of the BH army. It's just that I didn't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did you do next, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I went to my own village, and at the crossroads where the roads fork - one goes to the church and the other goes to the Zelenika house - I saw the body of Slavko Mendes who was an ambulance driver. His hands were tied behind his back and he was killed by a firearm. His hands were tied by a length of wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how was he dressed, sir? Meaning in a uniform or in plain clothes?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Uniform. He was an ambulance driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I'm going to show you some diagrams which I'd like you to look at.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: If I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could we start off with the one with an A in the right corner, which is 0293-7633, that's the ERN.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, do you recognise this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: This is a sketch that I drew showing -- well, there are some houses missing here, but you can see the school building. This is the road to Zelenika and my own village. Rajic next to the school building, and then further down, Ljubic, Kata, and Mata. The next house is the Perkovic's house, and then Mara Grubesa's house where she was killed. Luca and Janja Zelenika. Dragica Zelenika. And then the next house down the road is -- next to my own house, there's another house that belongs to me. And then the Zelic's house. And here is where the road forks off to Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's start -- or, before we start, who drew this map -- I'm sorry, diagram?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, does this -- this diagram follow the route that you took through the hamlet of Zelenika?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. That was where I went first and that's why I put the number 1 there. I went from the school up the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said that you saw a body of an ambulance driver --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- named Slavko Mendes. And could you just tell us where on that document --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Slavko Mendes, yes. It was -- it was hereabouts. There's something better over here, the one that is in colour. There's a monument that his wife had had erected for him near the school. You can see --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll get back to that shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But may the record reflect that the witness pointed to the square building without any name to the right of the school as the place where he saw the body of Slavko Mendes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I make a suggestion. It's going to be hard to read from --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This isn't. This isn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't want to interrupt the witness and perhaps he can explain later. But I just wanted to say that it's going to be hard to put it back together again if we're comparing the map to the record. What might be a good idea is if the witness was given a clean copy of this and he can mark it as he wants to, using his memory, to say where the bodies that he saw were located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's a good idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you put a 1 --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Which one are we going to use?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you put a 1 -- a circle, a 1, in the area where you saw the body of Slavko Mendes, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: This is not a house. I just put a box there so you know where the body was found. There is an old farming cooperative just further down the road, but this is where I found the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You put an X there. Could you put a 1 over that, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, where did you go next after you saw the body of Slavko Mendes?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We went to Domin Rajic's house. We found Ivo and Domin's wife, Ivka. That's the house next to mine on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you put a 2 there?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, what dead bodies did you find there?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Here is where I found Domin, his son Ivo, and his wife Ivka Rajic. Four or five metres further down from them was Zorka Glibo. She wasn't right next to the house but rather a short distance away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how Ivo was dressed?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Ivo was an HVO soldier. I can't remember what he had. I know he had a bulge on his head. He had been cracked over the head by someone or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And his mother, Ivka, and his father, Domin, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Local wear, traditional. They weren't wearing uniforms. They were plain civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And - am I wrong - was Ivka the mother of Ivo or the wife of Ivo?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: You're not wrong, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So Ivka was the wife of Ivo?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: His mother, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Domin was his father.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you said that you saw a third person or a fourth person there, a Zorka Glibo?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. Her body was lying about four or five metres from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you know who the Zorka Glibo was?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: She was Marko Glibo's wife from the village of Bobari, a village halfway between Here and -- what's it called, Budin. There were about three or four houses there because war was closing in and they went further down to Uzdol. One was out in the country and another was staying with Domin as a refugee.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how was she dressed? In a uniform or plain clothes?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Plain clothes, civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what was their condition? Were they alive or dead when you saw these four people?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: All dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What did you do after you saw these bodies? Where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I went to the house. About 40 or 50 metres from their house is Mate Ljubicic's house that was on fire. Mate Ljubicic was in front of the house and Kata Ljubicic, his bride, was behind the house. They were both dead and the house was on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: On the diagram could you place a 3 at that house.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Mate was right here and Kata was over there. She tried to run to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, was Kata Ljubic related to you in any manner?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: She was my godmother. That's what we call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see her often in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I saw her often. She lived near where I worked, near the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know if Mato or Kata Ljubic were members of the military?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Mato is an elderly person. Kata was a little, you know, before we brought bread -- she helped us knead dough for the bread. Then when we got new bread she left her old job because she was still quite young.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed, if you recall? Were they wearing uniforms or were they in plain clothes, civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Civilian clothes, plain clothes, both Mate and Kata.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after the Ljubic house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I headed down the road to my house and reached Kata and Stipo Perkovic's house. Kata's body was lying in the house; she was dead. Stipo had somehow managed to leave the house and he survived. He had managed to escape. And he didn't even realise that his wife had been killed, so he just took off without her.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can you please place a 4 on the Kata and Mato Perkovic house -- or Stipo Perkovic. Place a 4 on the diagram.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I've placed it where you can see the roof of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where was Kata located?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Kata was just outside the door. She was wearing black. She had thick-lensed glasses because her eyesight was very poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, where did you go after the -- after that house, sir, after the Perkovic house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I walked on down this road to this house over here Gorcic [phoen] Kovcalija's and Slavko's house had been set on fire as well as the barns. There was another barn that was on fire. There's another path leading to Grubesa's house. The barn was on fire, and people said that his wife, Mara, had burned alive in the house. She got locked up with their cattle inside the barn. The barn collapsed and then her husband later found her there. We entered the house, and we found her mother-in-law dead inside the house, Marica Zelic. She later died in a mental hospital near Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's take it one step at a time. Could you first put a 5 where Mara Grubesa's house was?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Grubesas -- Grubesas. This is Mara's house and the barn must be over here. Mara is right there. There's a path there for tractors, so the barn is on this side of the road and the house is the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The barn that was burning, were you able to enter it at the time?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No. There was fire all over the place. It had some sort of a tin roof which had collapsed due to the heat. You couldn't come anywhere near the barn.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ask anyone where Mara was?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We did. We asked her mother, the one we found at Pero's house, but she knew nothing. There was some sort of a creek behind the house. She took refuge there and she survived, but she didn't know things, she said. Mara was off to release the cattle from the barn and she came to grieve there. Her daughter Janja was also there. The soldiers called her to come with them, but she started running and was fired at. She -- she caught a bullet with one of her fingers, but she didn't even know about her mother, Mara.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was Mara ever seen after September 14th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, never. She was buried along with all the other victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, were her remains ever found in that barn?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Well, her husband said he'd found something. I have no idea what exactly he found. He wasn't clear about it. It was next to a wooden door. The barn had a wooden door. There was something there apparently where he claimed to have found something, but I really can't say myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is there any memorial there today for her, Mara Grubesas?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. Pavo, her husband, had the area cleared where the stable used to be. He said he would never build a new stable, a new barn, there. He had a granite slab placed there, 50 by 60 centimetres, carved her name in it and her year of birth and year of death. And the slab is still there as we speak, right next to where the stable used to be, the barn, and there are always flowers around the slab.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, where did you go after Mara Grubesa's house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I went on to Luca Zelenika's house and Janja's house which is after Palo's house. They're about 70 to 100 metres apart. Luca was lying dead outside the house, outside the door. She was an old woman aged over 60 and Janja was next to the wall. Her body was lying there. Apparently she had tried to run from one house to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could you put a 6 in the area where Luca and Janja Zelenika's homes were?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: This is where I found Luca, and Janja's body was on the other side. Luca was actually inside the house and Janja was near the wall outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, Luca, was she related to you in any way?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. She was my father's sister-in-law, and Janja was also a relative of my father's. They were his brother's children.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where did you go next, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I took the path to Dragica Zelenika's house. The house was on fire, so was the barn. There was an area covered with concrete next to the house. Dragica's body was there. She had been half burned. When the roof caved it, it probably caught her. She still had her socks on and her body was half burned. It was very close to the fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put a 7 at Dragica Zelenika's house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was she related to you?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, no relation. She did marry a relative of mine, though, but her maiden name had been Kovcalija. We were some sort of relation. Actually, her husband and my father are four or five times removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And just for the record, Dragica, Luca, Janja, three Zelenika women, you saw bodies; were these people dead or alive?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: All dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, where did you go after Dragica's house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I went to my own house. Pero Zelenika's house was on fire and so was the barn. I reached Josip Zelenika's house. I called out his name, Josip had made it. He was Janja's brother, but I couldn't find him. I passed someone else's house on the way to my house. I reached my house; it was open. I saw my daughter, Jadranka, lying outside on the floor. The door to the living room was open. I could see my father's body lying face down in the room, and my mother's body was on their marital bed and her forehead had been smashed to pieces with bits of brain plastered all over the wall and the ceiling. The top of her head had been blown away, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you put an 8 on the diagram where your parent's house was.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said when you walked in the house you saw your daughter first. What was her condition when you saw her?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: She was lying on her back gurgling, sort of trying to say something, but she couldn't. She was gasping for air. She was trying to breathe in and out. I was shattered. I had no idea what to do. I kissed her, but I could see that she wouldn't make it. And I took her over to my mother's room and laid her down on the bed. My father was quite heavy; he weighed over 100 kilos, so I left him lying on the floor because I couldn't lift his body.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: For the record, could you tell us your daughter's name?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Jadranka Zelenika, born 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your father's name, please?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Ivan Zelenika, born 1930.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And your mother's name?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Ruza Zelenika, maiden name Rajic, born 1931.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you leave the house sometime after that?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I had to. I knew that my neighbour, Ruza, was further down the road and her husband Stjepan, they used to play with my children. So something was telling me to go there. I reached their house. Our houses are about 100 metres apart. We didn't find them, though. A hand grenade had been thrown just outside the house and exploded there. We took the road down to the crossroads, and there was a tracksuit lying there that I recognised as belonging to the little Stipe. We found two hand grenades there and then automatic rifle, and we knew that they had been chased down the road to my house. Further down the road, Ruza's body was there next to the road; she had been killed. And the little Stipo that probably tried to run. He was wearing some sort of yellow pullover and shorts. He probably didn't have time to put his tracksuit on. Mara tried to run down the road to Here, and two or three metres before she reached the road, she was shot down dead. She was lying there face down. They were all dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, can we start off, can you put a 9 on the Zelic house, the one you went to and no one was home?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Number 9, and they were killed about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you put a 10 in the area where they were killed, you found the three dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, how old was Stjepan approximately, Stjepan Zelic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: He was one year younger than my daughter Jadranka; he was born in 1982. Marija was one year older than my daughter; she was born in 1980. They were a little larger than my daughter. My daughter was a little smaller than they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the mother's name was Ruza?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: The mother's name was Ruza Zelic, nee Dzalo. She was from Bobari, and she married a Zelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall if any of them were wearing shoes when you saw the three dead bodies, Marija, Stjepan, and Ruza?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No. Little Stipo was only in his underpants. Ruza had put a coat of some kind on. She put quite a few clothes on, but she was barefoot. The other young girl was barefoot. They didn't have time to take any clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where do you go next, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We then went towards the village of Kriz. That's where we set off to. We went to the village of Budin. Budin is between Zelenika and Kriz; there are four or five houses there. Not a single house had been set on fire or destroyed there. No one lived in it. Most of the people were in Austria. Then from the southern side of Kriz because the fire was opened from the northern side, from Krstic, we then went to Anica Stojanovic's house, also known as Brko.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. One second, sir. The diagram A that you've been drawing on, it is 0293-7663.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May that be offered, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P300.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What about the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There's both of them, Your Honour, the original and the one that he drew on. Can we offer both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the diagram that was marked with the same ERN will be Prosecution Exhibit P301.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to look at the next diagram which has the little B circled in the corner, which is 0293-7634 is the ERN number at the top. Could you look at that, please. Could you tell us which hamlet is depicted in that diagram?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: This is the hamlet of Kriz.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who drew this diagram, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I drew this diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And does this depict the route that you took into the village -- I'm sorry, into the hamlet of Kriz?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes, it does. We first reached Anto Stojanovic's house and then we continued into the village up to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just one question. Before you got to Kriz you said you went in the hamlet of Budin and that nothing was damaged or burning. And was anyone living there at the time?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, nothing was damaged. No one was living there. They probably knew that there was no one there. No houses or stables had been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, once you entered Kriz where did you go first, which house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We came from the southern side because there is a hill there, then we reached Anto Stojanovic's house. He is also known as Brko. He was an elderly retired man. Anto was dead, lying in front of his house, or perhaps 20 metres from his house in the direction of Budin. I don't think he had any footwear on. I think he was wearing thick socks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could you put a 1 over Anto Stojanovic's house or in the house itself?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: He was about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I see you've put an X where the body was.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: He was 20 or 30 metres from the house. He must have tried to flee in the direction of Budin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And from Anto Stojanovic's house, where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: There was some stables behind his house. We set off in the direction of Stojanovic; the lower part of the village is called Stojanovici. That's where we saw Ivka Zelenika, who had survived. She was there in a sort of orchard. She came out. She was crying. She didn't know who we were. She was afraid. She was just crying out, My son, I don't know anything. We then told her, Sit down. Let's see if there is anyone else alive. She said, I don't know anything. She was afraid. She didn't want to remain there. She wanted to go with us. Then we reached Anica Stojanovic, who had been killed. When she saw Anica, she was very distressed. We had to pour water over her. Anica had been killed in front of her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you put a 2 in the area where you met Ivka, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you put a 3 at Anica Stojanovic's house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said that you saw that Anica Stojanovic had been killed. Where was the body?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: It was on the road in front of the house. There's a path leading to the house itself. There's a bit of concrete in front of the house and then a path goes below the house, another above the house. She had been killed on the path. Her legs were to the side. Her head was facing upwards I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, was Anica related to anyone else who had been killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. She was the daughter of Kata Perkovic who had a pair of glasses. Her husband Stipo had survived. She got married in Kriz.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown photograph 0402-0932, ERN number 0402-0932.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: This is the village of Kriz.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see Anto Stojanovic's house there?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you please circle it and place a 1.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about the Anica Stojanovic's home?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Anica Stojanovic's home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And does that photo depict the Ratkic home?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. It depicts the new house because the old house burnt down to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you place a 3 there. And was the --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: You can see that it was constructed later on. The Dutch government was involved in this project.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, is that in the same location that the old house was?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: At the same place on the same foundations. They constructed a new house on the old foundations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And finally, can you see the Franjo and Serafina Stojanovic house in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: You can't see it very well here because their house is on the other side. There's a hill here and then the road goes around their house, but you can't see it now. All you can see are the stables at the top of Kriz, and this building is down below on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We'll use another photograph then for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could I offer that photograph, Your Honour, the original and the copy. And the copy with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objections.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the original of the photograph will be Prosecution Exhibit 306, and the one that was marked will be Prosecution Exhibit P307. And also the previous diagram, the second one that was shown with ERN 0293764 will be Prosecution Exhibit P302. And the same diagram that was marked in court will be Prosecution Exhibit P303.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, I've got a question to ask you, that is: What is the relationship between the two villages, Uzdol and Kriz? Kriz is part of Uzdol or are they separate places?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll have the witness explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And after that we might have a break before you come to the next section.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, we've talked about various hamlets. You started off with Zelenika. In what village was -- is Zelenika a hamlet, of what village?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: All these hamlets, Kriz and Zelenika, are in Uzdol and they all come under the name of Uzdol. If a child is born in Kriz or in Zelenika, he's registered as having been born in Kriz. That's the same case for Rajici or Budin. Uzdol has five or six hamlets and, some of the hamlets you have four or five houses and others you have nine or ten houses, et cetera. For example, you have Kranjcici, Gorni Kranjcici, Donji Kranjcici or Ljubunci, Memici, Nedzari [phoen], Glibe, Jurici, a lot of such villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour, if you would like to take the break at this time, that would be fine..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take the break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Still good morning. Now, when we left off we were in the village of Kriz and you had just left Anica Stojanovic's house. And where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: When we reached the house, Martin Ratkic's house, the house was on fire, the roof had fallen in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry, one moment. Let me get the diagram for you to look at. Sorry, sir. Sorry about that. You went to Martin and Kata Ratkic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to intervene.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: One moment, I'm sorry. My apologies for interrupting like this. I just wanted to check, has this document been tendered or not as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think he's referring to Exhibit B which is 02937634. I haven't tendered it yet. I haven't offered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. Because I think the witness has got more markings to make on it, that's all, and if it had been tendered, that was going to create a problem. But if it hasn't been tendered, there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P303.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There will be a few additional markings on it because I haven't officially tendered it yet. I think they did that because we moved ahead with the photograph. It has an MFI number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, can I just indicate that I'm happy with that and I don't object to that. In fact, it's very desirable that all the markings be on the one sheet and that's really why I jumped up now. If it has been tendered could I just put on record I don't object to the witness further marking that exhibit even though it has been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You indicated you went to Martin and Kata Ratkic's house and that it was burning. Were you able to approach the house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: The fire was quite intense. We thought that perhaps they had been set on fire, too. His brother's house is further down, the cellar was open, it was below the first floor. Kata and Martin were dead and Martin Ratkic had an ear that had been cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Lets take it one step at a time. You went to his brother's house, which was further down. Who was his brother's name?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Blaz, Blasko Ratkic. The houses are next to each other, very close to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you first put a 4 on Martin and Kata Ratkic's house on the diagram?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you put a box with a 5 where the brother Blaz's house was, Blaz or Blasko?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: That's about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said you went into the basement and you saw -- what did you see when you went into the basement of Blaza's house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We saw Martin and Kata. They were holding each other. They had been thrown on to each other and Martin didn't have one ear. Someone had cut his ear off.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were they dead or alive, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: They were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We couldn't go to Franjo Stojanovic's, also known as Franc, and his wife's, Serafina, because that was to the north, towards Krisaj [phoen], in the direction of Krstiste and there was an open space meadow, so we couldn't go home before nightfall. So we then returned by the church. There's a path that passes by the church from Anto Stojanovic's house --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One second. One second, sir. Before we move on to the next path, why couldn't you go to Franjo and Serafina Stojanovic's house? What prevented you from going there?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We couldn't go there because they were shooting from the hill called Krstiste. They were shooting, there was an open space there, and the houses were facing Krstiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever see Franjo and Serafina Stojanovic again?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I saw them when they took them to the school in the night, when they went to go to Prozor. They put them in lorries and drove to Prozor, but I didn't go to see them at night. They took them to the school and then a lorry came and took them to Prozor and to Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said they were taken to the school. Were they dead or alive when they were brought to the school in a lorry?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: They were dead. They were all dead. They were driven away in an open lorry, in a TAM vehicle and a lorry called a 110 lorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could you put a 6 where Martin and -- I'm sorry, Franjo and Serafina Stojanovic's house is on that diagram.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could we offer that diagram in the original at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original of that Prosecution Exhibit P302 and the diagram that's marked and called Prosecution Exhibit P303.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like the witness to please look at a photograph ERN number 0149-4700, 0149-4700.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 308.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what that photograph depicts? Sir, we have it in front of us.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: This is the village of Kriz.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, is that a fair and accurate representation of the hamlet of Kriz, which is part of Uzdol, as it appeared in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, is Franjo and Serafina Stojanovic's house depicted in that photo?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes, it is, it's down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher. Mr. Registrar, too, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please circle Serafina and Franjo Stojanovic's home.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: And there was a stable which burnt down. You can't see it here. It wasn't rebuilt and that's why you can't see it in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the house is circled and there is a line indicating where the stable is. Could we offer that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, stable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into the evidence, both the original and the marked one.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original will be Prosecution Exhibit P308 and the one that's marked Prosecution Exhibit P309.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were indicating that after you left the Stojanovic home you started heading towards another hamlet.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We didn't even reach Stojanovic's home on the first day -- I mean in the course of the day. It was only in the evening that Serafina and Franjo were brought there, and we left Martin Ratkic's house in the direction of Rajici, in the direction of the church and the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now just one quick matter before we leave. You said Franjo and Serafina were brought there in the evening. Are you talking about their bodies being brought to the school on the evening of September 14th?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. When it wasn't possible to open fire because there was an open space there and it was difficult to gain access to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said that you went to the village of Rajici next.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown diagram C which has an ERN number of 0293-7635, 0293-7635, with a circled C in the top right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 310.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And this is the third and last of the diagrams.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recognise this diagram?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell the Court what it depicts?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Here you can see the village of Rajici, the houses, the church, and an area between Kriz and the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who drew this diagram, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I drew this diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And does it depict the places that you visited in Rajici on September 14th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. Prskalo's house and Mara Rajic and Ivka. There were two other houses. But they were killed in these two houses, only these two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let us start with Rajici. Where did you go first once you went to the hamlet of Rajici?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: When we got there the first house there is Pero Prskalo's house and Jako Rajic's house. Pero's house is above the road. And Jako's house is down below but they are adjacent. Pero's house is a big house. It was on fire. The roof had caved in, the roof, the tiles, the bricks, everything. Next to the house there's a small truck path from the main road that they had built so they could reach their house by car. Their bodies were lying there, Luca Rajic and her husband Stanko, one facing up, the other down. They were each facing in a different direction I think. The old woman Sima Rajic was also there and her daughter Mara Rajic, the daughter of Sima Rajic. Jela Dzalo had died in the house. She was staying with the Prskalos as a refugee. She had three children. Her sister had come over from Austria and had managed to escape as far as the local shop where she was captured by the soldiers. She gave them some money and managed to escape with the children; they are alive and well in Austria now. Her husband Stanko, their son Mijo and her daughter whose name escapes me now -- Brigita. She was born in Austria so they gave her an Austrian name apparently. Brigita. They're staying with their aunt in Austria and with Jela's husband, Stipe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's take it one step at a time. First could you put a number 1 on this diagram where the Prskalo house is?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you please show us where you found the dead bodies of Lucija Rajic, Stanko Rajic, and Sima Rajic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: There's a path here. This is the main road. And there's a path next to the house and they were killed right there halfway down the path, not far from the house. The house had been burnt to the ground but it has been rebuilt. It's a very nice and big house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you put a 2 where those three bodies were located?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you indicated that Sima's daughter Mara Rajic was also lying dead. Could you put a 3 where that body was?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: It was nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You put a number 4. Could you change that to a number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you learned that Jela Dzalo died inside the house. Were any of her remains ever found?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, never. It was a big house; it was a big fire. Her sister says that she returned to the house because she had left something behind and she had come back to get it and she was killed. She never showed up again. They celebrated mass for her, as for everyone else who had been killed. Her children are still alive in Austria as well as her husband. He used to work in Austria before the war. He would sometimes come over. Her husband's name is Stipo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is there a memorial for her?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: There is at Uzdol for her and for the Grubesas woman. It's the same memorial as for all the other victims. It's a small memorial centre and it's the same memorial for everyone with their names stated, year of birth, and year of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after you went to the Prskalo house, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We went to the church. Jako Rajic's house was next to the road; it hadn't been set on fire. Sima and Mara Rajic's house, they must have run over to Jela's house, and they were found there, their bodies. But Jako's house had not burned down, it's just next to the road. Further down the road is Ivan Rajic's house and behind his house is Mijo Rajic's house. Mijo was outside the house killed at his own door-step here the road. His wife Ivka was inside. She was an ill woman. She had suffered a stroke and she was killed inside the house, whereas Mijo was killed outside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's do this first. Could you mark a number 4 on the diagram of Mijo and Ivka Rajic's house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that Mijo was just outside the house, Mijo was found dead just outside the house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Outside the house at his door-step, just outside the door on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said Ivka had had a stroke. Was Ivka able to walk in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, no she wasn't. She hadn't been able to walk for about ten years at least. She was bedridden. She hadn't walked for a great number of years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And about how old was she?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I think she was born in 1921. Mijo must be a year or two younger. She was born nearby. Her maiden name was Mendes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could that diagram be offered, the original and the marked diagram, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The diagram of ERN 02937635, the original, will be Prosecution Exhibit P304. And the same diagram which is marked in court by the witness will be Prosecution Exhibit P305.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May the witness now be shown a photograph having an ERN of 0402-0929, 0402-0929.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 310.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what that photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: You can see the village of Uzdol, Donji Rajici, you can see as far as Zelenike over there, my house, the garden. The Zelic's house. Right here you can see Rajici with the church, the school -- the two churches, the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, is the hamlet of Rajici a part of Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. The whole thing is Uzdol: Zelenike, Rajici, Kriz, Bobari, Pale. And down in the field there are houses, Gojko Maric's house, Stojanovic's house, more houses over there that you can't see in the photograph. It's all part of Uzdol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, is that photograph a fair and accurate representation of the hamlet of Rajici as it appeared and also parts of Uzdol as it appeared in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is the Prskalo house depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. It's been rebuilt.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was it rebuilt on the same location where the original house had been?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. The same spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you put a 1 over that house, please.

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is the home of Mijo and Ivka Rajic also depicted?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes. This one over here. This is Jako's house and this is Ivan and Mijo's is the third one in the middle. The third one, they're all below the road. Prskalo's is the only one that is above the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you put a 2 over the Rajic house?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: This last one was Stanko and Lucija Rajic's house but they were killed right here, near this house. This is Stanko's house, Stanko and Lucija's Rajic. And it wasn't burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let the record reflect that there is a line or slash mark near Stanko and Luca Rajic's house. Thank you. I'd like to offer that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house over here, this first house is Sima and Mara Rajic's house, the one next to Prskalo's house, Jako's house. Jako had died. Sima's husband and Mara's father.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original of that photograph is Prosecution Exhibit P310 and the one that is marked now is Prosecution Exhibit P311.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, may the record reflect there's a little U-shaped line to the right of circle number 1 which he indicated was Sima Rajic's house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sima and Mara's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after you saw -- you left Mijo and Ivka Rajic's house, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: We went down the road to the church. There is an open space here. We were fired at from the hilltop. They fired at us. We ran to the woods right here and we reached the area north of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you a few questions about some of the people you had seen killed. Other than Ivo Rajic at the first house you visited who was the young soldier that was lying dead, any of these other people that you saw killed, were any of them wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, none. All civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Of those people you had seen killed, had you ever seen in, let's say, August or September, had you ever seen any of these people dressed in a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In August or September of 1993, had you ever seen any of those people who were killed carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Near any of these people who were killed did you see any weapons?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I don't know. At that moment all I saw were dead bodies. I can't remember if there was anything else lying around. There was soldiers in the area, so some of them may have left their weapons behind. This is not something that I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were any of these people to your knowledge, any of these people who were killed, members of the HVO or any other military organisation?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I don't think so. They were all elderly people except Domin's son and Slavko, the ambulance driver. All of them were elderly persons, some retired, some plain old, women, grannies, children.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned Kata Ljubic. How long had you known Kata Ljubic?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I'd known her for a very long time. She was originally from Kriz but she married a man from Uzdol from Zelenike. It was up in the hill above Zelici, and they built a new house between the church and the school, and that's where they were killed, outside that house. Previously they had lived for about ten years near Glisina Brdo [phoen]. There was no road, so they built a small road leading to the place from the church to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether Kata was mobilised by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I know that at the beginning of the war she made bread using flour. We didn't have -- there was no food to buy and those women who were younger were not able to make bread. But this didn't go on for a very long time. After a while we stopped making our own bread and we were again supplied with bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when you said she made bread, whom did she make bread for?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: She made bread for HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how long --

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Some other ladies were involved in that, too, but I'm not sure. They would do this in their own homes, not in the schools where the soldiers were billeted. But each woman had an assignment. One had to make two breads per day, and another two or three loaves. They would work in the kitchen and they would take shifts, first shift, second shift, third shift, those who had been mobilised, rather young ladies, but I know nothing else about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long did she make bread, if you know?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I don't know. It could have been two or three days; it could have been as long as a month. We made bread ourselves until we got fresh supplies of bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know if she was making bread for the HVO in 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so, but by then we started receiving new supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Domin Rajic who you saw killed on that date?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: Yes, I know Domin. He had worked in Split, and once he had retired he returned in 1993 or possibly 1992. He hadn't been around for long, but he used to work in Split as a janitor with a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he was mobilised, sir, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: No, no. Domin wasn't, not that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a group called the home guard?

utterances.speaker: KAZO ZELENIKA
utterances.text: The home guard, that was later. They wanted some of the elderly people to make rounds of the village in the evening to see what was going on.
